brief:
Today is Push A, and it is the first one you have done at the new gym. That is the whole story of tonight's card.

Left alone, this app was about to ask you for 175 pounds on the smith incline press, four sets, on a smith machine that does not exist in the building you now train in. It would then have asked 180 on the chest press, a number that belongs to the old gym's stack. Both are gone from your card. Your recovery trainer objected to the smith figure on fatigue grounds and I agreed with it: the opener is now dumbbells, 40 for eight, then 45 for eight twice, three sets instead of four. Forty-five per hand is not a guess. It is what you pressed for eight, three sets running, on 27 August, and it is what the smith overhead press honestly became on 2 September when you did it with dumbbells. Fifty broke down to five reps that night, so we start under it. Tonight's job on that lift is to write down a real incline number for the first time.

The chest press is re-anchored to the only reading you have from the new machine: 2 September, 97.5, 127.5 and 157.5, eight reps each. I kept your load trainer's version, which does not raise the top weight at all — 157.5 stays — and only asks for the ten to twelve reps the program has always asked for. Your recovery trainer wanted a straight repeat at eight. I ruled against it because eight is below your own rep range and a second night of it earns nothing.

Rear delts go up. On 27 August you got fifteen, fifteen and fifteen at 90, which earns the step, and on 2 September you took it and got 100 for thirteen before dropping to 90. So tonight asks 100 for thirteen, 100 for twelve, then 90 for fourteen — the third set you did not get to that night. Overhead triceps sits at 55 for all three sets, which is exactly what you did on 3 August, and the whole task is finishing the third set there instead of dropping to 50.

One place I overruled your recovery trainer and want to tell you why, because it was arguing carefully and it was wrong. It wanted the rope pushdown cut to 27.5, reasoning that the new gym's cable stack must read lower. I checked. Your reverse-grip pushdown read 25 at the old gym on 23 August and 27.5 at the new one on 2 September, and your overhead triceps read 55 in both buildings. The cable stack is on the same scale in both places, so 27.5 is simply your reverse-grip weight, not a new-gym number. The rope pushdown goes to 45 for two sets — one notch below the 47.5 that actually collapsed on you on 17 August, over the two sets this slot now carries rather than three.

Now two things about the app itself that you should hear from me rather than work out yourself.

Your Legs B from Friday the 5th did not reach this repository until Sunday evening. That means yesterday morning's review was written for a Legs B you had already finished, and your phone would have thrown the whole packet away. The same thing happened the morning before with your 3 September Pull B. Nothing wrong reached you, but for three mornings running this review has been reading a log that is a session behind, which is why so much of it has been re-measuring instead of coaching. If the app is holding your sessions on the phone until you next open it, opening it on the way home would fix more than anything I can write here.

And your logs are increasingly being typed in afterwards rather than tapped as you lift. On 3 September nine of twenty sets share a twenty-four second window, and one set is stamped before the set that came before it. On Friday, both hip machine second sets landed under a second after the first, and both hanging leg raises landed twenty hours later. That is fine as a record of what you did. It just means those days carry no usable rest times, and a night with no rest times is a night I cannot tell hard from easy.

Housekeeping. Bodyweight has not been logged since 23 August, fifteen days ago, at 207. With the show on 1 March that is the one number I have no other way to get. Step on the scale this week. Easy cardio twice, twenty to thirty minutes.

Five Yes/No cards are waiting on your plan screen. Four are the same problem — sessions that still open with a lift named for a smith machine you no longer have. The Push A one is tonight's and it is the awkward one: there is no incline press anywhere in your exercise list, so the only honest swap available is assisted dips, and you skipped dips on 2 September, so that station may not exist there either. If it does not, answer No and tell me, because the real fix is adding an incline press to the list, and the panel cannot add one.

flags.note: Your card was about to ask 175 pounds on a smith incline press and 180 on the chest press — both old-gym numbers for machines you no longer use. Tonight's opener is dumbbells instead.

Meso 2, week 3 of 4, a build block. All three trainers reported; five disagreements, all settled, and one fatigue objection upheld.

proposals.why: Your new gym has no smith machine and your exercise list has no incline press at all, so tonight's opener becomes assisted dips at 4 sets of 8 to 12 — the only chest compound left in the list that needs no smith machine and no new load history, since it is bodyweight; answer No if the new gym has no dip station either and I will find you something else.

On 2 September you pressed dumbbells at 45 and 50 into a slot still named for a smith machine the new gym does not have, so this renames it to the dumbbell shoulder press you are actually doing — 4 sets of 8 to 10 instead of the smith bar's 6 to 8.

Pull B still opens with a smith row the new gym does not have and your list has no barbell row to rename it to, so it becomes the wide seated cable row at 4 sets of 8 to 10 — heavier and lower-rep than the same row on Pull A.

You already ran this slot with a barbell on 5 September and wrote so on the card, but it is still named Smith RDL and your list has no RDL, so it becomes the deadlift at 4 sets of 8 to 10 — same four sets you did, lighter and higher-rep than your Pull A sets of 5 to 6.

Carried over unanswered from yesterday: the cable lateral raise is your only side-delt work on Push A and it sits seventh of eight, so on 27 August the session ended before you reached it — this moves it to fifth, straight after the shoulder press.

overrides.reason: There is no smith machine at your new gym, so the 175 and 180 this card was about to print belong to a building you left. Do this on dumbbells: 40 for eight to find the bench angle, then 45 for eight twice. Forty-five is what you pressed for eight three sets running on 27 August, and incline is a stronger position than overhead, where 50 broke down to five reps on 2 September. Three sets, not four. Tonight is for writing down a real incline number, not defending an old one.

The 165, 172.5 and 180 this card wanted are the old gym's stack. Your only reading from this machine is 2 September — 97.5, 127.5 and 157.5 for eight each. The top weight here is unchanged from that night; the only thing asked is the ten to twelve reps your program has always asked for. If the numbers on the machine read differently, log what it says.

You paid for the jump to 17.5 on 27 August with reps — fifteen, fifteen, fifteen at the old weight became twelve, twelve, twelve at the new one. So the weight stays and the reps come back: one more per set before anything moves again.

A 45-pound dumbbell weighs 45 pounds in any building, so this is the one lift tonight the gym change cannot touch. You did eight, eight and eight on 27 August, which is the bottom of the range. Nine each before the weight moves.

You earned this one outright: fifteen, fifteen and fifteen at 90 on 27 August. You took the step on 2 September and got 100 for thirteen, then had to drop to 90 for fourteen and stopped at two sets. Tonight asks for the same two sets plus the third one you did not reach.

The card wanted 57.5 for three sets off a single set on 27 August. On 2 September you got 55 for eleven, then ten, then dropped to 50. This is 55 across all three, which is exactly what you did on 3 August. The job is the third set, not the weight.

Not logged since 17 August, and it faded inside that session — thirteen, twelve, then eleven. Same 10, one more rep on each set. It is the only side-delt work on this day, which is why there is a card on your plan screen asking to move it earlier.

This has been sliding for a month: 60 in July, 52.5 then a collapse to 47.5 for thirteen and eleven on 17 August. So it resets one notch below the weight that actually broke, over the two sets this slot now carries instead of three. Your recovery trainer wanted 27.5 on the theory the new stack reads lower; I checked and it does not — your reverse-grip pushdown read 25 here and 27.5 there, and your overhead triceps reads 55 in both.

dissent.progression: Hold the old figures — 175 for seven three times and 180 for eight — because reps went backwards at 175 on 27 August so nothing was earned, and the new gym's incline station has never been read.
dissent.recovery: Refuse the smith number entirely and establish a dumbbell baseline: 40 for eight, then 45 for eight twice, three sets.
dissent.why: Progression's own reasoning defeats it. It wrote that the new station has never been read, and then prescribed a load measured on a machine that does not exist in the building. He has had no smith machine since 2 September, by his own note. The one comparable transfer we have watched — smith overhead press at 105 to 135 on the bar, becoming 45 on dumbbells and missing at 50 — says the carried figure would have been roughly four times the honest one. Recovery also filed this as an injury veto in its first pass; I sent it back, it re-read its own file, found no pain or injury anywhere in the log, and refiled on fatigue grounds, which is the truthful label and one I am allowed to overrule. I chose not to.

dissent.progression: Re-anchor to the new machine's only reading and earn the prescribed rep range at an unchanged top pin: 127.5 and 142.5 for twelve, 157.5 for ten.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 2 September verbatim — 97.5, 127.5 and 157.5 for eight each — because the number is measuring the machine and not the man.
dissent.why: Both seats agree the old 165 to 180 is dead, so the disagreement is only about what to ask of the new reading. Recovery's fear is that a raise here is a guess, but progression does not raise the top weight at all — 157.5 stays exactly where he left it. What it asks for is ten to twelve reps, which is what this slot has prescribed all along and which he has not yet met on this machine. A second night at eight earns nothing in week three of a build block, and 97.5 and 127.5 were plainly the ramp up to the top set, not working weights.

dissent.progression: Take the step he earned: 100 for thirteen, 100 for twelve, then 90 for fourteen.
dissent.recovery: Roll back to 90 for fifteen three times, because three sets at 100 has never happened anywhere.
dissent.why: Recovery is describing an ask nobody made. Progression does not want three sets at 100; it wants the two he already produced plus the third set he skipped, at the 90 he dropped to himself. The raise was earned cleanly — fifteen, fifteen and fifteen at 90 on 27 August — and taken successfully on 2 September at the new gym, so this is not a cross-building guess. Undoing a raise a week after he earned it is the more expensive mistake here.

dissent.progression: 55 for eleven, eleven and ten — finish the third set at the weight, do not chase 57.5.
dissent.recovery: Drop to 50 for twelve across three sets.
dissent.why: Progression's prescription is not a raise. He produced exactly 55 for eleven, eleven and ten on 3 August, and 57.5 for twelve twice on 23 August. Recovery's 50 is below work he has repeatedly completed, and its worry about the new gym's stack does not survive the log: this lift read 55 at the old gym and 55 again at the new one on 2 September. Same scale, proven weight, one unfinished set to close.

dissent.progression: Cut to 45 for fifteen, twice — one notch below the 47.5 that collapsed, over the slot's current two sets.
dissent.recovery: Cut much harder, to 27.5, because the new gym's pushdown station read 27.5 on 2 September.
dissent.why: I checked recovery's premise and it is wrong. 27.5 is his reverse-grip pushdown weight, not a scale artifact: that lift read 23.75 to 25 at the old gym through July and August and 27.5 at the new one, which is a rep-earned step up, not a stack change. His overhead cable extension reads 55 in both buildings. The cable stack has not changed scale, so cutting a rope pushdown to a reverse-grip weight would ask a third of the right load. Both seats agree the lift needs cutting after 17 August; progression's is the cut the evidence supports.
